nina: Quick heads-up: rolled the sparse-prefetch optimizer to canary this morning. Short summary: p50 down ~15%, p95 down ~30%, projected infra token cost down ~35% for short-chat-heavy tenants.

todd: Nice! what's "sparse-prefetch" in one line?

nina: Lightweight predictor that pulls only hot key subsets (sparse vectors of KV indices) instead of whole prefixes. Paired with an adaptive merge that combines tiny concurrent requests into one decode when keys overlap. Low-risk: disabled for long sequences and high-entropy sessions.

anya: Canary numbers?

deploy-bot: Canary report (id: canary-sparse-2026-07-02): 90k requests, 70% chat, median seq 32, p50 40ms -> 34ms, p95 260ms -> 182ms, error rate unchanged 0.02% -> 0.02%. Dash: https://internal.redwood/perf/canary-sparse-2026-07-02

nina: Config we used (conservative):

```
prefetch:
  mode: sparse
  max_sparse_keys: 64
  session_min_turns: 3
  memory_pressure_disable_pct: 80
merge:
  enabled: true
  overlap_threshold: 0.35
  max_merge_window_ms: 5
```

todd: Any host impact? regressions?

nina: Small CPU uptick (~6%) on coordinator processes during peak; we added a local soft-cap for concurrent prefetches and fall back to full-prefix read under pressure. No customer-facing regressions in canary.

anya: Rollout plan?

nina: Canary -> 2% -> 15% (6h) -> 50% (24h) -> 100% (48h). Auto-rollback if p95 increases >5% or error rate delta >0.15%. Monitoring hooks and a canary smoke job are in place.

cost-bot: Projected monthly savings if fleet-wide: 28-38% infra token spend reduction for convo tiers. Logged under COST-2026-07-SPARSE.

todd: Please add a one-paragraph blurb for next all-hands and mark model-onboarding so owners know sparse-prefetch can change cache hit patterns.

nina: Will draft slides and a short docs post with the config+dash links.

anya: Nice win, thanks team :tada:
